tests.what: Premium welcome redesign with social proof above the fold
Refreshed winback layout leading with brand USPs
Elevated welcome redesign with repeated offer callouts
Social proof versus savings framing for repeat cart viewers
Refreshed checkout design focused on risk-free try-on
Moving code delivery above body copy in welcome

heartbeat.title: Lead with the strongest motivator, early
heartbeat.body_html: Both winners this month pointed the same way. In the Welcome Flow, moving the code delivery above the body copy lifted click-to-open among incentive-driven non-customers, and in the abandoned cart series, leading with a high-volume social proof signal beat the usual savings framing for shoppers who'd already seen the offer twice. The transferable lesson: put the single strongest reason to act at the top, before anything else competes for attention. We're now applying that ordering logic across other flows to see where else it holds.

narrative.html: Flow revenue came in at $62,672, down 41.9% on last month, with revenue per email delivered easing from $0.882 to $0.314. The drop tracks a quieter store overall, and flows still held 15.1% of total store revenue, right in line with the 15-17% band they've kept since May.

Flows continue to do the heavy lifting per send. At $0.314 per email versus $0.019 for campaigns, each flow email earned 16.5x more, and flows drove 60% of all email revenue off a fraction of the volume.
Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes ran at 0.352% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.005%, well inside safe territory, which keeps the flows landing in the inbox where they earn.

Campaigns sent 16 this month at $0.019 per email. These are run in-house and that's your call, but if it would help we're always happy to take a look at the campaign side and share a few ideas, no strings attached.

monthly.title_sub: Flows held 15.1% of total store revenue in a softer trading month, earning 16.5x more per email than campaigns.

tests.what: Direct second-touch nudge versus softer nostalgia-and-urgency framing

heartbeat.title: Proof holds its ground
heartbeat.body_html: This month's single test in the Back-In-Stock flow saw the control hold against a more casual, friend-style nudge. That is a genuine result, not a null one. The current messaging is now validated as the stronger performer, so we keep the revenue it earns and lose nothing by trying. This is the asymmetry that makes the testing program compound: every winner is banked permanently, every challenger that falls short costs nothing, and the flows keep improving over time regardless of any single month's strike rate. Running one of the most comprehensive automated flow-testing setups in the industry means we are always learning which version of each message earns most, and confirming a control is as useful as crowning a new winner.

narrative.html: Flows delivered $107,880 this month and held their share of total store revenue at 16.8%, up slightly from 16.0% last month. The revenue figure eased 9.2% versus June, but the share holding steady tells us flows kept pace with the store rather than losing ground.

Every flow email earned $0.882, against $0.026 for campaign emails. That is 33.9x more revenue per email from the automated flows we manage, and flows accounted for 65% of all email revenue this month.

Flow RPR softened from $0.983 to $0.882, worth keeping an eye on next month. Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.422% of delivered and spam complaints at just 0.006%, so the audience health underneath the flows remains sound.

On the campaign side, 16 sends went out in-house at an RPR of $0.026. There looks to be headroom there, and if it would help we're happy to take a look at the sending strategy at any point, no obligation.

monthly.title_sub: Flows brought in $107,880, holding at 16.8% of all store revenue despite a modest month-on-month dip.
